cards.title: One tasks mirror per window: the runner reads the store, not a second bus and poll
acceptance: her window starts the strip (startTasks) and the runner (startTaskRunner) with a counting fake follow -> the bus is followed exactly once (today: twice, tasks.ts:68 and task-runner.ts:139)

a bus that is refused at once and reconnects 10 times inside 1 s of fake clock, both started -> GET /tasks is read at most once per REREAD_MIN_MS in total (today the runner reads on every reconnect: 10 reads)

start with one daemon row `running` that no window runs and one `queued` -> the orphan is finished `failed` with ORPHANED exactly once, before the first POST /tasks/claim, and exactly one GET /tasks precedes that claim (today 3: the store's load, sweepOrphans, reread)

a task.changed frame {status:'killed'} for a task the runner runs -> its request aborts, no /finish is posted, its cards are withdrawn and declined, and useTasks shows the row killed - all from the one frame
a list read that no longer contains a task the runner runs (and is not finishing) -> the runner kills it, no /finish posted
a task.changed frame {status:'queued'} -> the runner claims (POST /tasks/claim) without waiting for any poll

the runner stops while the strip still holds the store -> the store keeps following and reading; the strip stops while the runner runs -> the runner still hears the next task.changed (counted holders, one follower)
Main with no runner (only SurfaceTasks holding the store) -> reads, frames and the 404-is-no-tasks rule behave exactly as today (tasks.test.ts unchanged and green)

cards.body:
## Summary
Her window mirrors GET /tasks twice: the tasks store (strip and Main) and the task runner each follow the bus, each read the list, and only one of them learned the throttle. Make the store the one mirror per window and have the runner subscribe to it.

## Description
`stores/tasks.ts` states the rule - the bus is the fast path, the list is the truth, a reconnect read is held to one per REREAD_MIN_MS because a daemon with no bus refuses at once. `stores/task-runner.ts` re-implements the same mirror for its own needs (kill on a non-running frame, claim on a queued one, sweep orphans once) with its own followBus, its own 15 s poll and an unthrottled read on every reconnect. Under a refusing bus followBus reconnects every second and calls `connected()` each pass, so the runner reads GET /tasks once a second while the store, beside it, reads once per 5 s. That is the parity drift a duplicated rule produces (realtime-events / push-vs-refetch-reconciliation: events are advice, the read is truth - one read path, exercised once). The move: `tasks.ts` exposes a counted subscription that hands a listener each applied frame and each settled list read; the runner takes a holder (`startTasks()`) and listens, dropping `follow` and `every` from RunnerDeps. The orphan sweep runs on the first settled list after start, so it still precedes the first claim.

## Flow
- startTaskRunner -> startTasks() holder + onTasks({frame, list})
- frame -> taskChanged (kill / claim) exactly as today
- first list -> sweepOrphans(rows) then reconcile + tickRunner; later lists -> reconcile (kill missing) + tickRunner
- stop -> release the holder; the store's last holder ends the follow

## Expected impact
One bus stream and one throttled read path per window instead of two; the once-a-second read storm under a refusing daemon closes; a future change to how tasks are mirrored lands once. Kill, claim and orphan semantics are pinned unchanged by guard cases.

## Evaluation
Claim: the runner and the store share one mirror without changing kill/claim/orphan behaviour.
Before: 4 of 8 acceptance cases pass (the four guards)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases in task-runner.test.ts and tasks.test.ts
Result: better
Gate: none

cards.title: The dock's due notice opens the staged review in place: prepare, skip, later
shared_surfaces: docs/adr/0131-a-chore-comes-due-as-a-staged-review.md (addendum: the dock line opens the review in place; §8 and §12 otherwise unchanged)
acceptance: a notice on show, pressed -> one GET /adopt/cases/<case>/review; the dock state becomes {kind:'reviewing', review} with the review's lines in LINE_ORDER; nothing is POSTed

reviewing, Open and prepare -> POST review {due_at, answer:'prepare'} exactly once, deps.open once per http(s) portal, deps.hand(command, {caseId, scheduled:true}), no /run; the next queued notice takes the dock
reviewing, Skip this one -> POST review {answer:'skip'}; the next queued notice takes the dock
Later -> no POST at all; the next queued notice takes the dock; the same (case, due_at) is not shown again in this window

a queued notice whose review was answered elsewhere meanwhile (GET review answers review.answer set, or review null) -> dropped before it is drawn, never stamped seen, and the next one takes its place (proactive-nudges / notice-delivery-decoupling: re-validate before late delivery)
three notices in one poll -> the dock line says '<title> is due · 2 more due'; after one is handled it says '· 1 more due'; the last says no count
the review read fails (daemon down) -> state {kind:'failed'} with one sentence, the notice stays on show, and 'Open the chore' still navigates to the chore's page as today
the seen stamp is sent once per (case, due_at), only after the dock has drawn the line (ADR 0131 §8, unchanged)

cards.body:
## Summary
Today a due chore costs five steps: press the dock line, land on the playbook's topic page, scroll to 'Make it yours', find which of its cases is due, then read and press Open and prepare. The dock has the case id and the review is a pure, no-model read. Open the staged review in the dock itself, with its three answers, and say how many more wait.

## Description
The dock line keeps its place and its rules (never a raised window, seen when drawn). Pressing it reads the case's review (GET .../review, the direct fetch due-poll already uses, so first paint pays nothing) and draws ReviewView in place: what to check first, then Open and prepare (openAndPrepare with the Playbooks module's open and hand, loaded on press), Skip this one, Later (put away with no answer: the review stays open on the topic page, where it is today), and 'Open the chore' for the full page. Before a queued notice is drawn its review is re-read: one answered elsewhere is dropped unstamped, not announced as false news (notice-delivery-decoupling). The line carries the queue's size, answering ADR 0131 §10's 'eight dock lines, shown one at a time' with a visible count. The staged-review rule stands: the person still sees the lines before preparing, and nothing is sent until she presses send (README §2, ADR 0131 §12).

## Flow
- poll -> queue -> re-validate head -> draw line '<title> is due · N more due' -> stamp seen
- press -> reviewing (GET review) -> Open and prepare | Skip | Later | Open the chore
- each answer -> next notice; failure -> one sentence, notice stays

## Expected impact
A due chore goes from five steps across two surfaces to two presses in the dock; stale notices stop; the person sees the backlog size. Operator-visible on every scheduled chore.

## Evaluation
Claim: the dock enters the review, answers it and moves on, without a navigation.
Before: 2 of 8 acceptance cases pass (the two guards)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases in console/due-notice.test.tsx and scenes/chores/due.test.tsx
Result: better
Gate: none
